dedupe_keys.name: fca access to cash coverage in the uk quarterly

description: The FCA publishes quarterly data on how close people in the UK live to places where they can get cash. It gathers the locations of brick-and-mortar and mobile branches of designated banks and building societies each quarter and monthly data on ATMs and the Post Office network, supplemented yearly by cashback locations and branches of large non-designated providers, with temporary closures, opening hours and accessibility. Straight-line distances from residential addresses to the nearest access point are aggregated to output areas, local authority districts and countries. Each publication has downloadable Excel tables: counts of access points by type and nation, the share of population within 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 miles by region and rural or urban area, and the underlying local authority data for the coverage maps, with Tableau maps. Publications run from 2021 Q1; 2024 Q2 is the baseline of the new access to cash regime and is not comparable with earlier quarters. Data.gov.uk lists them under the Open Government Licence. Caveats: point locations are not published, some are postcode centroids, and straight-line distance overstates coverage. For simulation it measures the resilience of physical cash infrastructure, useful for payment outage and digital exclusion scenarios. Related catalogue records include the ECB payments statistics and the BoF-PSS2 payment and settlement simulator.
name: FCA access to cash coverage in the UK (quarterly)
provider: Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), with the Payment Systems Regulator
spatial_resolution: local authority district, region, rural and urban
temporal_coverage: 2021 Q1 to 2024 Q2 (publications listed on data.gov.uk)
